articles.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw (CVE-2026-98432)
articles.context: On October 25, 2026, the National Vulnerability Database published CVE-2026-98432, a vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP stack
articles.full_text:
What happened?

On October 25, 2026, the National Vulnerability Database published CVE-2026-98432, a vulnerability in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP stack. The flaw is a use-after-free: when a server handles a retransmitted SYN for a connection request, it can read IP options from memory that has already been freed. This can lead to a crash or memory corruption. The Linux kernel fix defers freeing these IP options until after an RCU (read-copy-update) grace period, so no thread can still be using them when they are released.

Okta's response

Security Patching: All Okta and Auth0 environments are fully patched or mitigated against this issue.

No Evidence of Exploitation: To date, Okta and Auth0 have observed no evidence of exploitation.

Do I need to do anything?

For customers running Okta Access Gateway (OAG), we recommend upgrading to the latest version and restarting your appliance to ensure the patched kernel is loaded.

articles.title: Node.js Project: November 11 Security Releases
articles.context: js project released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across core modules, including authentication bypasses in TLS certificate handling, memory-safety...
articles.full_text:
What happened?

On November 11, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing multiple vulnerabilities across core modules, including authentication bypasses in TLS certificate handling, memory-safety defects in HTTP request parsing and HTTP/2 session handling, denial-of-service conditions, and information disclosure in proxy configuration, 8.0.5 (CVE-2026-123863, CVE-2026-123864, CVE-2026-123865, CVE-2026-123866, CVE-2026-123867, CVE-2026-123868, CVE-2026-123871, CVE-2026-123872, CVE-2026-123874, CVE-2026-123875, CVE-2026-123877, CVE-2026-123828, CVE-2026-123829, CVE-2026-123862, CVE-2026-123873, CVE-2026-126051)

Okta's response

No Evidence of Exploitation: Our assessment identified no exploitable exposure in Okta or Auth0 production environments.

Do I need to do anything?

Customers using the Auth0 AD/LDAP connector: We recommend downloading and installing the latest version, v8.0.5.

Customers using Auth0 Actions: We recommend updating the runtime to Node 22 and deploying your changes. Customers already on Node 22 do not need to redeploy.

Customers using Okta or Auth0 Node.js SDKs: We recommend updating your Node.js runtime to the latest patched version across:

node-auth0

nextjs-auth0

express-openid-connect

passport-auth0

node-jsonwebtoken

okta-sdk-nodejs

okta-oidc-middleware

okta-jwt-verifier-js.

References

Node.js November 2026 Security Advisory

articles.title: Qubole supply chain attack exposed AWS, Entra ID, and Okta credentials
articles.context: The attacker was said to have exploited integrations that remained trusted even after some organizations had stopped using the platform
articles.full_text:
An attacker has abused AWS cross-account IAM roles to access multiple customer environments, steal data, and harvest credentials in a supply-chain attack that ran between October 14 and October 26.

Researchers from Wiz, working with Sentra and Mandiant, said they observed an attacker using IAM credentials for Qubole’s AWS account to assume roles in customer environments.

The compromised credentials allowed the attacker to access customer AWS accounts that had previously established cross-account access permissions with Qubole. The access was used to enumerate cloud resources, retrieve secrets and configuration data, download files from Amazon S3, and test credentials belonging to affected organizations.

Sentra, which initially identified suspicious activity across several customer environments, said the campaign affected dozens of Qubole customers. The attacker was said to have exploited integrations that remained trusted even after some organizations had stopped using the platform.

Attackers used Qubole’s AWS credentials

Qubole integrations rely on cross-account Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles. Customers typically create roles that allow identities belonging to Qubole’s AWS account to assume them, with an External ID serving as an additional check against unauthorized access.

The attacker had credentials that could satisfy this requirement.

Wiz said the first suspicious activity was observed on October 14, when an IP address associated with Mullvad VPN attempted to assume customer integration roles from AWS account 805246085872, which Qubole uses for its platform operations. The requests used an IAM user identified as AIDA3W7DIFLYOLTK63SFS.

Most of the activity that came later originated from an OVH-hosted VPS, 57.129.54[.]120. The attacker also began using a second IAM identity associated with Qubole’s AWS account on October 18, alongside another Mullvad VPN address.

All malicious role-assumption requests identified by Wiz included the required External ID and succeeded. Many of the targeted roles had seen no legitimate Qubole activity during October, but their permissions remained active.

After gaining access, the attacker enumerated cloud resources, including S3 buckets, databases, EC2 instances, security groups and IAM identities. The intruder also accessed AWS Secrets Manager, Systems Manager Parameter Store and Lambda function configurations to retrieve credentials and other sensitive information.

Attackers stole data, and hosted a suspicious Linux image

The attacker used the assumed roles to download data from Amazon S3, enumerating accessible buckets and objects before retrieving their contents. In some instances, Wiz said, entire buckets were downloaded in individual sessions.

Credentials discovered in the compromised environments were subsequently tested using TruffleHog, a secrets-scanning tool. These included AWS access keys, Microsoft Entra ID service principal credentials and Okta OAuth client credentials.

Sentra reported identifying more than 100 passwords and keys read within minutes, alongside thousands of additional credential records contained in downloaded files. The company also said the attacker performed no write operations in the observed environments, suggesting an operation focused on data theft.

Wiz also found a bootable Linux ISO image, named “sso_agent.iso,” hosted on the attacker’s OVH infrastructure. The image collects system information, communicates with the server over TCP port 23458, and can execute remotely supplied shell commands. Its configuration suggests it may have been designed to target Windows systems, the researchers said in a blog post.

Wiz, however, did not find any deployments of the image and could not confirm whether it had been used against victims.

The campaign has not been attributed to a known threat group.

Tightening integrations and third-party access will help

Wiz recommends that organizations using Qubole review AWS CloudTrail records dating back to October 1, 2026, across all accounts containing integration roles. Investigators should look for suspicious AssumeRole activity originating from Qubole’s AWS account, particularly requests from non-AWS infrastructure and IAM identities identified in the disclosure.

Subsequent activity involving Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, Lambda and S3 should also be investigated, Wiz noted. Other recommendations include removing unused third-party integrations and narrowing trust policies to specific vendor IAM principals rather than allowing an entire external AWS account to assume a role. Organizations should also restrict role assumption to documented vendor network ranges using AWS source IP or VPC endpoint conditions.

articles.title: Node2Shell: Node.js Brotli flaw (CVE-2026-111497)
articles.context: js project released fixes for a Brotli decompression flaw (CVE-2026-111497, "Node2Shell")
articles.full_text:
What happened?

On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released fixes for a Brotli decompression flaw (CVE-2026-111497, "Node2Shell"). The flaw is an out-of-bounds write that can crash a process or allow remote code execution (RCE).

Okta's response

Security Patching Services: The change has been deployed across the production environments of both Okta and Auth0.

No Evidence of Exploitation: To date, Okta and Auth0 have observed no evidence of exploitation.

Do I need to do anything?

Customers using Auth0: We recommend updating the runtime version in your Auth0 tenant settings or in your Action configuration to Node 22, then deploying your changes. Customers already on Node 22 do not need to redeploy.

Customers using Auth0 SDKs with Node.js: We recommend downloading and installing the latest version.

Customers using the ad-ldap connector: We recommend downloading and installing the latest version.

Reference

Aikido Security, Node2Shell: Node.js Brotli vulnerability allows remote code execution (CVE-2026-111497)

articles.title: Okta and Auth0 are removing trust in the eMudhra emSign ECC Root CA – G3
articles.context: On October 17, 2026, a researcher reported that the private keys of eight intermediate eMudhra certificate authorities were generated with insufficient entropy and could be...
articles.full_text:
What happened?

On October 17, 2026, a researcher reported that the private keys of eight intermediate eMudhra certificate authorities were generated with insufficient entropy and could be derived from their public certificates. The derived private keys can be used to issue certificates for any domain, and software that trusts the eMudhra root will accept them.

Mozilla, Google, Apple, and Cloudflare have blocked the affected intermediates. Mozilla has removed the emSign ECC Root CA – G3 from its trust store, and Chrome will remove it on October 27, 2026. eMudhra has revoked the intermediates.

Okta’s response

Okta and Auth0 are removing trust in emSign ECC Root CA – G3 and the eight affected intermediates across our services.

Security Patching Services: The change has been deployed across Okta’s production environment. The change is continuing to roll out across Auth0 production.

No Evidence of Exploitation: To date, Okta and Auth0 have observed no evidence of exploitation.

Do I need to do anything?

Only if Okta or Auth0 connects to a server you control and that server's certificate chain includes the eMudhra emSign ECC Root CA – G3. Inbound access to Okta and Auth0, including sign-in, is not affected.

The case to check is a non-browser connection or webhook that calls your own API, such as an Okta Inline Hook or Event Hook, or Auth0 Action, Custom Database connection, or Auth0 Federated Connection.

These connections may not have shown you any error before now. Run

openssl s_client -showcerts -connect <your-host>:443

and look for "emSign" in the chain. If you find it, replace the certificate with one from another trusted CA. Connections to that endpoint will fail once our change is applied to your tenant.

References

eMudhra Statement on distrust of select Global TLS Intermediate and one Root CA

Google - Protecting Chrome and Android Users from Compromised eMudhra Intermediate CA Certificates

Mozilla - Protecting Firefox users following the compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates

articles.title: Okta's Response to PHP2Shell
articles.context: Okta tested the publicly available proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits against Okta Access Gateway in its default configuration, and none achieved code execution
articles.full_text:
On October 21, 2026, industry-wide third-party critical PHP pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) were disclosed, both with CVSS scores of 9.2.

Okta tested the publicly available proof-of-concept (PoC) exploits against Okta Access Gateway in its default configuration, and none achieved code execution.

Okta’s Response

Cloud services: Not affected. Okta and Auth0 cloud service platforms are not affected by these vulnerabilities.

On-premise software: Okta Access Gateway (OAG) requires a patch. Customers should upgrade to Okta Access Gateway version 2026.44.0.

Action for Okta Access Gateway (OAG) Customers

Customers running Okta Access Gateway appliance versions prior to 2026.44.0 should upgrade to version 2026.44.0. For complete vulnerability details and remediation guidance, refer to the Security Advisory:

PHP Runtime Vulnerabilities Affecting Okta Access Gateway CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619

Action for Auth0 and Okta SDKs users

For actions required and developer guidance, please refer to the appropriate KnowledgeBase article:

PHP Critical Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619)
